A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, determine which represented billed revenue (invoices) is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with source-native identifiers, amounts, and association disposition.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entities_in_scope: counterparties named on invoices and contracts
exclusions: expired statements of work treated as inactive contracts
invoices omitted solely because identity linkage is uncertain

world_true: invoice exists with invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, and status as recorded in sources
contract exists with a source-native contract identifier
contract text contains or does not contain specific clause types (change-of-control consent/notice, change-of-control termination, assignment consent/notice/restriction)
contract or statement-of-work temporal status (e.g., expired vs not expired) as grounded in source dates or explicit status
purpose_policy: acquisition-relevant condition: clause requires consent or notice on change of control, permits termination on change of control, or requires consent/notice before assignment (including affiliate-only assignment or competitor-assignment prohibition)
active contract: an expired statement of work is not an active contract for inclusion
qualifying invoice: invoice whose counterparty is linked to a contract that is active under purpose policy and contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition
association asserted vs unresolved: whether invoice billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently joined

epistemic_requirements: Report invoice and contract identifiers exactly as they appear in authoritative sources
Assert association only when billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently associated
Do not treat missing or uncertain identity as a negative contractual finding
When association cannot be made confidently, include the invoice with association=unresolved rather than omitting it or asserting a join
Ground contractual clause findings in contract source text, not inferred from counterparty similarity alone
allowed_unresolved_states: association between invoice billed name and contract counterparty (association=unresolved)

completeness_expectations.must_enumerate: every invoice that qualifies under purpose policy (active contract with acquisition-relevant condition), including those with unresolved association
completeness_expectations.must_not_omit: qualifying invoices solely because identity linkage is uncertain
completeness_expectations.may_remain_partial: contract_id on unresolved rows when no confident contract link exists, provided association is marked unresolved and limitation is explicit in output
completeness_expectations.sorting: complete invoice list sorted by invoice_id

purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: expired statement of work is not an active contract
purpose_specific_policies.row_inclusion: invoice associated (asserted or unresolved) with an active contract containing at least one acquisition-relevant condition
purpose_specific_policies.identifier_rendering: use source-native invoice_id and contract_id strings without invented canonicalization

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, report whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records, or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.entities_in_scope: every commercially relevant name or record that must participate in linking CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates for a relationship

required_output_shape.ordering: links sorted by left ascending, then right ascending

world_true: CRM account record exists with crm_account_id and account naming fields
billing record exists with billed_name as recorded on invoices
registry row exists with company_number and legal/trade naming fields
contract file exists with filename and counterparty naming text
name strings may differ in legal-form variants while referring to the same registered entity
distinct registry entities may share similar trade names without being the same legal entity
purpose_policy: SAME_ENTITY: confident judgment that two identifiers denote the same legal counterparty
DISTINCT: confident judgment that two identifiers denote different legal counterparties
UNRESOLVED: insufficient evidence for same or distinct judgment
mechanical same-entity: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as same without further evidence
no similarity-only merge: superficial name similarity alone does not justify SAME_ENTITY
required link coverage: links needed to connect CRM account, its billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry rows for that relationship

epistemic_requirements: Permit explicit unresolved identity; absence of a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (distinct) judgment
Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar
Ground SAME_ENTITY and DISTINCT judgments with evidence; default to UNRESOLVED when confidence is insufficient
Include every link required to connect CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates for each commercially relevant relationship
allowed_unresolved_states: pairwise identity between any two scoped identifiers (epistemic=UNRESOLVED)

completeness_expectations.must_enumerate: every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
completeness_expectations.must_not_omit: required relationship links because identity is uncertain—mark UNRESOLVED instead
completeness_expectations.may_remain_partial: individual pairwise judgments may remain UNRESOLVED where evidence is insufficient
completeness_expectations.sorting: complete links list sorted by left then right

purpose_specific_policies.merge_policy: no global merge on string similarity alone
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_same_entity: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name
purpose_specific_policies.similar_trade_name_not_same: distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party
purpose_specific_policies.required_link_pattern: crm account ↔ billing billed name ↔ governing contract ↔ registry candidate(s) per commercially relevant relationship
purpose_specific_policies.orientation: class_rank over identifier types when establishing required links

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under purpose criteria, listing open invoices, governing contracts, obligation kinds, and dependency status.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
exclusions: expired contracts as sources of current dependency
one-off paid historical invoices without an active continuing contract

required_output_shape.identifier_forms: same as Purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)
required_output_shape.ordering: dependencies sorted by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

world_true: invoice status (open vs not open) as recorded in billing sources
contract active vs expired status grounded in source dates, renewal mechanics, or explicit contract text
contract contains exclusivity commitment, term auto-renewal clause, or rolling term continuing unless notice is given
counterparty identifiers refer to CRM, billing, registry, or contract records
purpose_policy: current commercial relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
commercially dependent: both (1) current commercial relationship holds and (2) active contract contains at least one of exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term
status dependent: purpose criteria satisfied with resolvable identity joins
status unresolved: identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved—report as unresolved rather than false/non-dependent
expired contracts do not create current dependency
historical one-off paid invoice without active continuing contract does not create current dependency

epistemic_requirements: Use Purpose B identifier forms for counterparty references
When identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report dependency status as unresolved, not as non-dependent
Ground obligation_kinds in active contract text or explicit renewal mechanics, not inferred solely from counterparty naming
Only include obligation kinds drawn from the closed vocabulary: exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term
allowed_unresolved_states: dependency status when invoice–contract–counterparty identity joins required by Purpose B are unresolved (status=unresolved)

completeness_expectations.must_enumerate: each contract-centric dependency row where purpose criteria are met or where dependency cannot be resolved due to identity uncertainty
completeness_expectations.must_not_assert_false: do not mark non-dependent when the blocker is unresolved identity—use status=unresolved
completeness_expectations.may_remain_partial: open_invoice_ids may be empty when relationship is contract-only but current via auto-renewal or rolling term
completeness_expectations.sorting: dependencies sorted by contract_id; obligation_kinds sorted ascending within each row

purpose_specific_policies.historical_invoice_only_excluded: one-off paid historical invoice without active continuing contract does not satisfy current relationship
purpose_specific_policies.identity_dependency: relies on Purpose B identity judgments; unresolved identity forces status=unresolved
purpose_specific_policies.row_inclusion: active contract with declared obligation kind and evaluable (or explicitly unresolved) current relationship
